title: Boss: the release train
summary: Name artifacts, promote through environments and run a pipeline with cleanup stages.

steps.title: The release train
steps.body: You are building the core of a small pipeline runner for a team that ships an API several times a day. Each piece below is one thing every real CI system does.

steps.title: Traceable artifact names
prompt: Write `string ArtifactName(string app, string version, string sha)` returning `app-version-shortsha`, where the app name is lower-cased
and the SHA is cut to its first **7** characters.
starter: string ArtifactName(string app, string version, string sha)
steps.solution: string ArtifactName(string app, string version, string sha) => $"{app.ToLowerInvariant()}-{version}-{sha[..7]}";

steps.title: Promotion
prompt: Environments are promoted in a fixed order, e.g. `["dev", "staging", "production"]`.
- returns `null` when `current` is the last one,
- throws `ArgumentException` when `current` is not in the chain (a typo must never deploy somewhere random).
hints: `IndexOf` returns -1 when the item is missing.
template: Dojo.Check("production is the end", NextEnvironment(dojoChain, "production") == null, "expected null");

steps.title: Cleanup always runs
prompt: Real pipelines have stages that must run **even after a failure**: tearing down a test database, uploading logs.
Write `List<string> Run(List<(string Stage, bool Passes, bool Always)> stages)`:
- before any failure, every stage runs: `"name: ok"` or `"name: FAILED"`;
- after a failure, normal stages log `"name: skipped"`, but `Always` stages still run and log ok/FAILED;
- a failing `Always` stage also fails the pipeline;
starter: List<string> Run(List<(string Stage, bool Passes, bool Always)> stages)
solution: List<string> Run(List<(string Stage, bool Passes, bool Always)> stages)
hints: Add the final summary line after the loop.
template: Dojo.Eq("green run", new List<string> { "build: ok", "cleanup: ok", "pipeline: passed" },
Dojo.Eq("cleanup runs after failure", new List<string> { "build: ok", "test: FAILED", "deploy: skipped", "cleanup: ok", "pipeline: failed" },
Run(new() { ("build", true, false), ("test", false, false), ("deploy", true, false), ("cleanup", true, true) }));
Dojo.Eq("failing cleanup fails the run", new List<string> { "build: ok", "cleanup: FAILED", "pipeline: failed" },
